## About these materials

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Citation statement
Please cite these materials as: Middleton, S., Verheyen, S., & Von Grebmer Zu Wolfsthurn, S., (2026). *Strategies in leadership* [Quarto slides]. LMU Open Science Center. [https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-open-research/leadership-open-research/strategies-leadership/](https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-open-research/leadership-open-research/strategies-leadership/)
:::

**Welcome!** These materials focus on **how to take action and address challenges** within Open Research. Awareness of our own spheres of influence is an important step towards positive change. These materials put into practice the **skills learned about effective leadership** using **case studies** that featuring challenges such as doing a preregistration and navigating large-scale collaborations. Equipped with a diverse set of strategies, Open Research leaders can then more confidently apply them to own research and teaching contexts.

The case study series on leadership in Open Research is co-developed by the LMU Open Science Center and the Framework for Open and Reproducible Research Training ([FORRT](https://forrt.org/)).

*Case studies:*

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em;"}
| Case study | Key themes | Where to find this |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Contributorship under tension | Authorship decision making, CRediT (Contributor Roles Taxonomy), power dynamics | click [here](https://zenodo.org/records/22307117) to access |
| Paulo’s preregistration problem | Preregistration, supervisor-student relationship, self-advocacy | click [here](https://zenodo.org/records/22307709) to access |
| Alex’s open code dilemma | Generative AI, reproducible code | click [here](https://zenodo.org/records/22306455) to access |
| Finn’s struggle to choose a method(ology) | Qualitative research methods, academic rigor | click [here](https://zenodo.org/records/22308007) to access |
| Listening beyond the protocol: Roya’s experience with cultural ways of knowing | Qualitative research methods, research ethics | click [here](https://zenodo.org/records/22308238) to access |
:::

### Who are these materials for?

- **Aspiring open research instructors**
- **Future open research train-the-trainers** and **educators** in higher education (e.g., universities, colleges) and
- **Self-learners** 

with familiarity about open research challenges, issues and tools, as well as a strong familiarity with leadership roles and skills and CRediT roles.

### Prerequisites

<div style="font-size: 0.8em;">
| Prerequisite | Description | Where to find this |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Basic familiarity with Open Science practices | Examples: R, Quarto, Git, GitHub, preregistration, Open Access etc. | [Click here to get familiar with Open Science first](https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-student-track-OS/) |
| Foundational understanding of leadership roles and key skills | Leadership in Open Science: Skills, values and culture | [Click here to get familiar with leadership in Open Science first](https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-student-track-pedagogy/leadership-open-research/leadership-skills-culture/) |
| Knowledge of CRediT roles | CRediT - Contributor Roles Taxonomy | [Click here to get familiar with CRediT roles first](https://credit.niso.org/)) |
</div>

### Learning objectives

At the end of this session, you will be able to ...

- **Examine** approaches to addressing challenges in Open Science from multiple perspectives to increase breadth of knowledge.
- **Discuss** and **propose** actionable and equitable strategies to address challenges in Open Science as a way to relate to own leadership contexts and build up collective problem-solving skills.
